summary: @servicetitan/microfront preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes bundled 727KB obfuscated payload
details: The package's package.json declares a preinstall script that runs setup.mjs on every npm install. setup.mjs is written with obfuscator.io-style renamed identifiers (hex-named variables, string-dictionary indirection wrapping fs/https/child_process/zlib) and downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it (including a hand-rolled pure-JS ZIP extractor fallback and a musl detection branch so it works without host unzip/powershell), chmod +x's the Bun binary, and then execFileSyncs Bun against a sibling file math_init.js in the package directory. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated bundle (obfuscator.io-style string-array rotator plus char-map decoder, prefaced with a '// @bun @bun-cjs' marker) that is never shipped as readable source. Invoking a freshly-downloaded alternate JavaScript runtime to execute an opaque bundled payload at install time is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern; running the payload under Bun (rather than the installer's Node) evades Node-oriented static and AV scanners. A microfrontend library has no legitimate reason to fetch a second JS runtime or execute an obfuscated 727KB blob during install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
